name: THS4631 (single high-voltage, high-slew-rate, wideband JFET-input op amp)
tagline: A ±15 V JFET-input op amp with 210 MHz GBW and 1000 V/µs slew. It is a cult DAC I/V and buffer part in Japan, praised as airy and transparent once it is stable.
technology: TI's JFET-input high-speed voltage-feedback op amp; the datasheet calls the input stage JFET. Single channel, unity-gain stable: 325 MHz bandwidth at G=1, 210 MHz GBW. Runs on ±5 to ±15 V (10–30 V single supply). SMD only: SOIC-8 (D), HSOIC-8 PowerPAD (DDA; 'SOIC-PP' in Rev B) and HVSSOP-8 PowerPAD (DGN; 'MSOP-PP' in Rev B). Standard single-op-amp pinout: 2 = IN−, 3 = IN+, 4 = V−, 6 = OUT, 7 = V+; 1, 5 and 8 are NC. TI's documents disagree about the thermal pad. Rev B, and the layout text of the current Rev C, say the PowerPAD is 'electrically isolated from all pins and the active circuitry', recommend grounding it, and allow any potential from VS− to VS+. The new Pin Functions table in Rev C says the pad is 'internally connected to V−'.

reputation.summary: A niche cult part in the Japanese DIY and op-amp-rolling scene. It is mostly used for I/V after current-output DACs, and in headphone amps and buffers via DIP-8 conversion boards. One Ameblo blog title calls it 'the rumoured op-amp' (噂のオペアンプ). Shirokuma sells it pre-mounted on a dual 8-pin DIP board. Users report extended highs, air and transparency when it is not oscillating. A Zigsow review calls it a 'tsundere honours-student character' (ツンデレ優等生キャラ). TI's datasheet lists 'Current DAC output buffer' as an application. No Audio Science Review or other audio-band measurements are known to this record.
sonic_descriptors: 'tsundere honours student' (ツンデレ優等生): excellent once stable
typical_uses: DIP-8 op-amp rolling via conversion boards (e.g. Shirokuma dual board)
Headphone amp op-amp swap (e.g. Elekit TU-HP01, per the xgender-isao blog)
caveats: Oscillates easily in rolling and adapter use. Japanese users report needing an output Zobel network. TI's datasheet warns that large feedback resistors oscillate with the input capacitance and recommends a feedback capacitor, which matters for I/V stages.
Runs hot: 12.5 mA typ and 14.5 mA max quiescent current per channel in Rev C (11.5 typ / 13 max in Rev B), about 0.375 W idle at ±15 V. A dual adapter carries two chips.

The thermal pad connection is ambiguous. The current datasheet's layout text says the PowerPAD is electrically isolated, recommends ground and allows VS− to VS+. Rev C's pin table says the pad is internally connected to V−. Tying the pad to V− satisfies both readings.
SMD only, so socket use needs an adapter. It is a single, so it replaces a dual only on a dual-conversion board.
Noise is specified only above 10 kHz, and there is no audio-band THD+N spec.
Parts shipped after the March 2025 datasheet (Rev C) may be re-characterised silicon. The listening impressions (c. 2018–2020) predate this.

revision_history.changes: Related-products table changed. Input impedance changed from 10^9 || 6.5 to 10^9 || 3.9 (Ω || pF). Figure labels corrected from RL=499 Ω to RF=499 Ω. Large-signal transient figures and the EVM schematic added.
Tstg corrected to −65 °C to 150 °C. No electrical changes were listed.

New TI format, with Pin Functions and ESD tables. OPA656 related-product values updated. 0–70 °C columns deleted. 0.1 dB flatness with CF=8.2 pF changed from 38 to 6 MHz, and 20 MHz without CF added. Static output current changed to 180 mA typ, 120 mA min at 25 °C and 90 mA min over temperature. Iq max changed from 13 to 14.5 mA (25 °C) and from 14 to 15 mA (over temperature). 'Updated graphs with new silicon data'. Changes not listed: Iq typ 11.5 to 12.5 mA; the pin table says the thermal pad is connected to V−; package names changed to HSOIC/HVSSOP.
Revision history from Rev A (March 2005) to Rev B: in Absolute Maximum Ratings, Tstg changed from '65°C to 150°C' to '–65°C to 150°C'.
Performance specs revised for a new manufacturing process ('new silicon data'). TI E2E thread 1514297 asks whether Rev C applies to all ICs or only newly ordered ones.

silicon_changes.when: Published in SLOS451C (March 2025). Rev B (Aug 2011) was still current in 2019, and TI's PSpice model dated 2020-11-02 still uses Rev B Iq and Isc values. No PCN was located, and the physical change date is unknown. The Sep 2023 PDN20230907001 discontinued only the D and DGN tube SKUs; that is a SKU action, not evidence of a die change.
silicon_changes.identification: By datasheet only. SLOS451C (Rev C, March 2025) says 'Updated graphs with new silicon data' and carries new limits; SLOS451B (Aug 2011) describes the legacy part. TI E2E thread 1514297 ('THS4631: Revision C - Relevant to all IC's or only to newly ordered ones') attributes the changes to a new manufacturing process. The top marking is unchanged ('4631' on D/DDA, 'ADK' on DGN in both the 2017 and 2025 addenda), and no date-code cutoff or PCN was found. The '.A'/'.B' orderable suffixes are TI-wide and are not evidence of a die change.
silicon_changes.summary: Rev C re-characterises the THS4631 on 'new silicon data', and on E2E TI says the performance changes come from a new manufacturing process. TI recommends omitting the feedback capacitor in new designs that use the new silicon. Output current rises sharply (98 to 180 mA typ), quiescent current rises (11.5 to 12.5 mA typ; 13 to 14.5 mA max), and 0.1 dB flatness with CF = 8.2 pF is re-specified from 38 to 6 MHz. The new pin table ties the PowerPAD to V-, while the layout text still says isolated. Headline specs are unchanged: 7 nV/rtHz, 210 MHz GBW, 1000 V/us, +/-500 uV Vos max, 100 pA Ib max. Whether the die was also redesigned is not stated.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: No listening or measurement comparison of old and new lots was found. Expect more idle heat, stronger static drive and a different response with feedback capacitance. The part is already oscillation-prone in I/V stages, so Zobel and CF values tuned on old parts may need re-checking; TI now advises leaving out CF in new designs. The Japanese impressions (c. 2018-2020) predate Rev C.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: pinout, package and headline AC specs are unchanged. But higher Iq, a changed compensated-loop response and the ambiguous pad potential can upset marginal thermal or stability designs, or adapters that ground the pad. Tie the pad to V-.
silicon_changes.verification: Two searches. They confirmed SLOS451C (Mar 2025) and found TI E2E 1514297, where TI attributes the Rev C changes to a new manufacturing process and advises omitting CF for the new silicon. This supports a real silicon change and moves the kind from pure datasheet-respec to process transfer. A candidate PCN (20240826006.0) that surfaced could not be tied to the THS4631 and is not cited.

counterfeit_notes: No THS4631-specific counterfeit reports are known; this pass did not search for them specifically. Genuine markings are '4631' on SOIC-8 (D) and HSOIC-8 PowerPAD (DDA), and 'ADK' on HVSSOP-8 PowerPAD (DGN). A DDA part must have an exposed pad underneath. The THS4631D and THS4631DGN tube SKUs have been obsolete since PDN20230907001 (Sep 2023), so 'new' stock under those part numbers from brokers is old or suspect. Hobbyists usually buy the part pre-mounted on DIP adapters (e.g. Shirokuma) or as bare DDA parts (e.g. eleshop.jp). Prefer authorized distributors. The marking cannot tell pre- and post-2025 silicon apart.
alternatives: THS4601: TI ±15 V FET-input, 180 MHz, 100 V/µs, 5.4 nV/√Hz, unity-gain stable. Listed in the THS4631 Related Products table.
OPA627: ±15 V difet, 16 MHz, 55 V/µs, 4.5 nV/√Hz. The audiophile benchmark; listed in the Related Products table.
OPA656: ±5 V FET-input, 230 MHz, 400 V/µs, 6 nV/√Hz. Low-voltage only.
OPA657: ±5 V FET-input, decompensated (min gain 7). Not a drop-in for unity-gain I/V use.
LF357 (LF357H metal can): the classic decompensated JFET part the Japanese community compares it with.
OPA828: modern ±18 V JFET-input audio/precision part (catalogued separately). A calmer, lower-power ±15 V I/V choice.
open_questions: Is Rev C's 'new silicon data' a real die, process, fab or leadframe change? Is there a PCN, and from which date code?
Is the DDA/DGN pad internally tied to V− on current parts? Rev C's pin table says yes; its layout text and Rev B say it is isolated.

Rev C is internally inconsistent: the Features list says 95 mA against 180 mA typ in the table; the history's '−40 °C to +125 °C' conflicts with the table's −40 to 85 °C; and the absolute maximum of 150 mA is below the 180 mA typical output current.
Which exact revisions do the Kyohritsu, Octopart (DGN), DigiKey media and alldatasheet copies hold? Only search-summary hints were available.
When did the E4/G4 variants and the DDAR reel become obsolete, and under which PDN?
There are no Audio Science Review or other audio-band measurements, and it is unknown whether Japanese adapter vendors now ship Rev C silicon.
e_n at 1 kHz is not tabulated.

claims_confirmed: The THS4631 datasheet SLOS451C is dated 'DECEMBER 2004 – REVISED MARCH 2025' (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/slos451c/slos451c.pdf).
The TI symlink serves the THS4631 'High-Voltage, High-Slew-Rate, Wideband FET-Input Operational Amplifier' datasheet; no newer revision was seen (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ths4631.pdf).

SLOS451A is 'REVISED MARCH 2005' and SLOS451B is 'REVISED AUGUST 2011'; the search summary names an Octopart copy as SLOS451A (https://datasheet.octopart.com/THS4631D-Texas-Instruments-datasheet-150388.pdf).

The current datasheet's layout text says the PowerPAD is electrically isolated from all pins and the active circuitry, recommends a ground connection and allows VS− to VS+ (https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ths4631.pdf?ts=1759211980946).
TI PDN20230907001 (7 Sep 2023) lists THS4631D and THS4631DGN for discontinuance, with a last-time buy (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/5545/PDN20230907001.3.pdf).
